text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Socialist party platform calls for reduced work hours, higher labour charges for firms, expresses skepticism about European single currency.
-- Finance Minister to discuss with local authorities solutions to maintain regional branch network of CIC amid growing opposition to planned privatisation.
-- Daewoo Electronics chairman Soon-Hoon Bae says in an interview that he would have to create a new plant to face increasing demand in Europe if bid on Thomson Multimedia is rejected.

-- Ailing state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade says bank needs two years to get ready for privatisation. The paper quotes Financial Times report that Finance Ministry asked U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs to approached potential bidders in Europe but no one was interested in the bank in its current state.
-- Price distortions in auto sector between European countries and France are coming to an end, as French makers cut prices to fend off competitors, study shows.
-- Court raps former Credit Lyonnais subsidiary SDBO for providing "excessive support" to businessman Bernard Tapie.
-- French Treasury to exceed 1996 borrowing programme.
-- British group NatWest to develop investment banking activity in France.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe says taxes on diesel fuel will rise no faster than inflation, after lorry drivers demonstrated against sector difficulties.
